native-device: the loader's ADT rebase of the RAMDisk property worked well enough for the kernel to configure md0/rmd0 over 0x8000 bytes at FFFFFFF008974000 and to make md0 the BSD root (major 1, minor 0); vfs_mountroot returned, VFS_ROOT and devfs_kernel_mount ran, with no panic.

native-device: the kernel panicked with a data abort at pc 0xfffffff0074a1444 (esr 0x96000005, far 0x110300e4, x8 0x110300e0) in bsd_init's e1s touch init, before load_init_program; no SWEET userspace banner, no initproc line.

source-review: that pc is _e1s_touch_init+0x174 (pinned kernel.no-storage symbol table); far and x8 are E1S_GPP9_DAT and E1S_GPP9_CON of 0003-e1s-touch.patch, whose gpio_rd() dereferences a physical-address macro instead of the ml_io_map'd base; the driver honours e1stouch=0.
not_established: Whether the ramdisk bytes at that address are intact, whether mockfs maps /sbin/launchd to the raw Mach-O, whether exec of an ad-hoc-signed init is permitted with cs_enforcement_disable=1, and whether PID 1's console text reaches loader_log: PID 1 was never started.
Whether e1stouch=0 is sufficient to reach load_init_program (later drivers in bsd_init: battery, camera probe, rtc, may fault too).
The attribution of the abort to _e1s_touch_init is a source-review reading of symbols and a patch; it has not been confirmed by a run with e1stouch=0.

The timed loader_return_after=8 return (both NAT-063 and NAT-066 returned through the panic path), the live kprintf -> loader_log path (dump 1 at checkpoint 21 was empty again), and the absolute kernel clock rate.
findings: The ramdisk path works up to the BSD root: the NAT-065 design (RAMDisk property + rd=md0 + rebase in the loader) is sufficient for the kernel to configure md0 and mount it as root on the phone.

The next obstacle is a driver defect in the project's own e1s patches, not the root path: e1s_touch_init reads GPIO registers through physical-address macros. The command line can skip it (e1stouch=0); e1sbattery=0, e1scam=0 and e1srtc=0 skip the other optional e1s drivers.

The kernel text reaches the host only through the return path (dump 2); a PID 1 that stays alive would not be seen. The probe init exits by itself within about 1 s, which is why its outcome would still arrive.
